name: Galitzenklamm
kurzbeschreibung: Galitzenklamm gorge near Lienz in East Tirol is a thundering natural ravine nestled at the foot of the Lienz Dolomites, featuring footbridges, via ferratas, and a forest park.
preis: Gorge admission applies; via ferrata climbing gear and aerial ropes course require extra fees
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from mid-May to late October, 09:00 to 18:00
beschreibung:
Überblick

The dramatic Galitzenklamm gorge is situated just a few kilometres west of the sunny alpine town of Lienz, where the cascading Galitzenbach stream rushes into the Drau River at the base of the jagged Lienz Dolomites. Renowned as one of East Tirol's most evocative natural monuments, the ravine offers an exhilarating showcase of roaring cascades, polished bedrock potholes, and sheer vertical cliffs. Over millennia, glacial meltwaters carved an intricate canyon through ancient rock strata. A masterfully engineered water educational pathway comprising suspended timber catwalks, cable suspension footbridges, and rock-hewn viewing galleries leads visitors safely alongside the thundering torrent. Beyond passive sightseeing, the gorge has grown into a versatile outdoor adventure arena: demanding via ferrata iron-way routes traversing directly above the churning foam, an extensive treetop obstacle forest park, and a children's water play park entertain visitors of every generation.

Route & Anforderungen

The standard self-guided circuit along the water trail measures roughly one kilometre and takes about 45 to 60 minutes of leisurely walking. Guarded wooden boardwalks and stone steps gently ascend into the chasm; while well maintained, damp rock conditions necessitate steady footing (unsuitable for wheeled strollers). Climbers can tackle six designated via ferratas spanning varied difficulty gradings (from family-friendly A/B to extreme grade E) bolted directly into the canyon's vertical gneiss. Standard flat shoes or light hiking sneakers with non-slip rubber soles suffice for the water pathway, whereas via ferrata adventurers strictly require a certified helmet, harness, and shock-absorbing lanyard kit, which can be rented on site.

Besuch & Anreise

Motorists travel via federal highway B100 (Drautalstraße) between Lienz and Sillian, following signage for Amlach and Galitzenklamm. Extensive free vehicle parking is located directly beside the gorge entrance pavilion. Cyclists can pedal directly to the gorge along the flat, paved Drau Cycle Path (Drauradweg R1). Rail passengers alight at Lienz main station and connect with local VVT bus line 962 departing straight to the Amlach Galitzenklamm stop.

Tipps

Visit during warm midsummer afternoons: the fine aerosol mist atomized by the pounding waterfalls produces exceptionally crisp, invigorating alpine air that revitalizes the senses. The cozy snack station at the canyon entrance serves delicious East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen dumplings on its shaded terrace.
